findings.explanation: The Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit is Splunkbase app 2890, not 617, and is installed on the search head, not delivered through a Universal Forwarder. Splunkbase 617 is not in the repository catalog.
findings.quote: Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit (MLTK) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the Splunk Machine Learning Toolkit as Splunkbase 2890, installed on the search head that runs fit, and remove the Splunkbase 617 and Universal Forwarder wording.

findings.explanation: The SPL reads license_usage.log (type=Usage) from index _internal. According to the repository's platform health guide, splunk_resource_usage belongs to the _introspection index and records per-process CPU, memory and disk usage, not license volume.
findings.quote: `index=_internal sourcetype=splunk_resource_usage` OR License Usage Report view
findings.suggested_fix: Name the real source: `index=_internal source=*license_usage.log type=Usage` (field b for bytes), collected on the license manager.

findings.explanation: implementation says to alert on the upper confidence bound, but the SPL compares the point forecast `predicted(gb_used)` to `license_limit_gb`. It never uses upper95. Visualization also promises 'days until projected overage', which the SPL does not calculate.
findings.quote: Alert when the upper confidence bound crosses the licensed capacity threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the SPL compare `upper95(predicted(gb_used))` with the licence limit, or change the text to say the point forecast is used. Add a days-until-overage calculation or remove it from visualization.

findings.explanation: The text never says where the licensed capacity value comes from or how to define `license_limit_gb`, which the SPL needs. Splunk's license size is not in license_usage.log Usage events.
findings.quote: Alert when the upper confidence bound crosses the licensed capacity threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the licence limit input, for example a lookup or macro with the daily quota in GB, and show how to add it to each row.

findings.explanation: None of the scenarios names a real cause of a wrong forecast. Real ones are a short history that cannot support seasonality, onboarding of a large new source, one-off backfills or re-indexing, and a licence change.
findings.quote: Health checks in `_internal` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: less than a few weeks of usage history, bulk onboarding or re-ingestion spikes, licence size changes, and month-end batch peaks.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `license_limit_gb` is never defined in the search, so `'predicted(gb_used)' > license_limit_gb` compares with null and `over_license` is always 0. The alert can never fire as written.

The title promises 'with Seasonality', but the fit command sets no explicit period (for example a 7-day period for weekly cycles). Check whether StateSpaceForecast detects the seasonality on its own, and whether the 365-day history needed for monthly patterns is searched.

summary: A sensible license-forecast idea whose app ID and data source description are wrong, and whose SPL compares the forecast with a field that is never defined. The alert rule in the implementation (upper confidence bound) does not match the SPL (point forecast).
